title: Introduce lane-fusion attention kernel with KV striping and async batcher
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Reduced p99 per-token latency by ~18% for long-sequence (>4k) generation; added lane-fusion attention kernel, KV striping policy, and an asynchronous continuous-batcher with adaptive windowing. Backwards-compatible API. Opt-in via runtime flags.
description:
Context and motivation: Long-sequence generation workloads (4k+ tokens) observed tail latency spikes under mixed-service traffic. Existing blockwise kernels and single-shard KV cache placement cause uneven GPU utilization and hot spots in the scheduler. This PR introduces a new attention kernel (lane-fusion) that fuses QK/KV micro-ops across contiguous head lanes, combined with a KV striping policy to distribute persistent KV shards across GPU slabs, and an async continuous-batcher that performs non-blocking windowed assembly of request batches.

Design summary: lane-fusion kernel consolidates the inner QK and value gather into a single CUDA path when sequence layouts align (most common in long, steady-generation workloads). KV striping maps persistent KV cache entries into N logical stripes per GPU slab to avoid single-slab hot allocation and to allow concurrent prefetch/eviction streams. The async continuous-batcher runs as a lightweight coroutine loop in the serving thread pool and exposes an adaptive window controlled by observed p95 latency — the window grows under low-latency headroom and shrinks on SLO pressure.

What changed (high level): commits: - Add lane-fusion attention CUDA kernel with fallback paths for misaligned sequences. - Implement KV stripe_manager with placement heuristics and async prefetcher/evictor. - Add async_continuous_batcher (Rust) with configuration knobs and integration with smart-routing. - Bench harness and perf tests for long-sequence steady-state and mixed-concurrency profiles. - Docs and runtime flags for opt-in and telemetry.

Checklist: - [x] Kernel correctness tests (unit and fuzz) - [x] Microbenchmarks for QK and gather paths - [x] End-to-end RLHF-style generation bench - [x] CI builds and GPU smoke tests - [x] Telemetry: added per-stripe allocation metrics and batcher window gauge

Benchmarks (CI harness on p4d.24xlarge, 32-batch concurrency mixed with 80% short/20% long requests): - Baseline (prior main): p50=18ms, p95=143ms, p99=212ms, throughput=1.0x - This PR (lane-fusion + striping + async batcher): p50=15ms, p95=118ms, p99=173ms, throughput=1.18x. Improvements are most pronounced on steady long-sequence tails.

Operational notes: the new KV striping is opt-in (runtime flag: --kv-striping=enabled, stripes=4). Lane-fusion requires models with contiguous head memory layout; runtime performs a capability check and falls back automatically to existing fused kernels otherwise. Async batcher is enabled by default in this branch but gated behind an internal feature flag until we validate in staging.

Testing and rollout plan: staged rollout: enable in perf-canary cluster (50% traffic) for two days, collect stripe allocation heatmaps and batcher window metrics, then enable for Dedicated pools with controlled capacity. Telemetry dashboards added under Redwood Console -> Runtime -> LaneFusion: per-model p99, stripe-utilization, batcher-window.

Known limitations: - Small-sequence workloads (<=128 tokens) see negligible benefit; batcher may slightly increase median under high burst traffic until adaptive window converges. - Striping increases meta-memory overhead (small constant per-stripe).

Related: ENG-3172 (scheduler improvements), ENG-3320 (kv eviction policies).

review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Can we add a compatibility check so lane-fusion doesn't get selected for legacy models?
Maya Chen: Added capability probe in runtime/attn/select_path.cc and fallback coverage in unit tests (see commit a3f9bf0).
Priya Desai: The stripe_manager looks good, but can eviction be prioritized for low-hit stripes?
Maya Chen: Yes — stripe_manager exposes a priority hint; default policy is LRU-per-stripe, I added an API to inject custom priorities for canary experiments.
Marco Bell: Microbench shows a regression for batch size=1 on short sequences; is that expected?
Maya Chen: Expected. Async batcher has an initial windowing warm-up; we added a fast-path bypass for batch_size==1 in this patch to limit regressions.
Aisha Rahman: CI GPU smoke failed once due to a flaky memcpy path, fixed in e9b1c2f, re-ran and all checks passed.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after telemetry and docs updated.
